newsitem.title: USA: Sun Microsystems shares rise after report.
newsitem.headline: Sun Microsystems shares rise after report.

text.p: Shares of Sun Microsystems Inc topped the Nasdaq's most-active list on Thursday, rising $2.81 to $31.06 after the company reported stronger-than-expected fiscal second quarter earnings.
Trading volume topped 20 million on the Nasdaq market.
Analysts said the share price rose after a flurry of increased earnings estimates for the year.

The company late on Wednesday surprised Wall Street with earnings of $0.46 a share in its second quarter. That was four cents above analysts' average estimate, according to First Call, and compare with earnings of $0.32 per share a year earlier.
Net income in the most recent quarter rose 41 percent to $178.3 million and surged to a record $2.08 billion.

Goldman, Sachs analyst Laura Conigliaro raised her earnings estimates to $1.80 a share from $1.70 for fiscal 1997 and to $2.20 from $1.95 for fiscal 1998, noting Sun's strengthening presence in the computer industry.

"With all signs pointing to strong momentum which should continue to be boosted by aggressive new product cycles and ongoing price/performance improvements, we can see how Sun's revenue growth should be able to move above the 20 percent level," Conigliaro said in a research note.

Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones raised his rating on the stock to buy from hold. He increased his earnings estimate to $1.77 a share from $1.73 for fiscal 1997, and to $2.10 from $1.96 for fiscal 1997.

Jones said in a research report the company was well positioned for "above-trend earnings growth," reflecting its introduction of its UltraSPARC server from a year ago and the perception of long-term advantage from its Java programming language.
